notes: Every cup begins as a fruit. Before coffee is a bean, it is a cherry on a tree.
Every cup begins as a fruit. Before coffee is a bean, it is a cherry on a tree.
Harvested at ripeness At peak ripeness, the cherry is ready for picking. Its fruit protects the coffee seeds within.
Harvested at ripeness At peak ripeness, the cherry is ready for picking. Its fruit protects the coffee seeds within.
Natural process The whole cherry dries with its fruit intact. The dry outer husk then breaks away, revealing seeds still protected by parchment. Whole-cherry drying · an alternative route
Honey process The soft fruit skin peels away to reveal the seeds. Some fruit mucilage remains on the coffee during drying. Mucilage retained · one processing route
Washed process Water carries away the loosened mucilage, exposing the solid, parchment-covered coffee seeds beneath. Mucilage removed · an alternative route
Removing the parchment Once dry, the brittle parchment is cracked and hulled away to reveal green coffee. Natural coffees also lose their dried fruit husk.
Selected. Sorted. Graded. Green coffee is prepared to an agreed buyer specification.
Roasting Heat transforms aroma, structure and flavour.
Ground for brewing Roasted coffee is ground to the particle size the brewing method needs.
From origin to the cup. One journey. Green coffee, roasted coffee and filter coffee.
